evidence: AssignTaskUseCase.execute and MarkTaskDoneUseCase.execute both call this.finder.findInProject(input.projectId, input.taskId), so the 'task belongs to project' rule lives only in TaskFinderService.findInProject.
AddTaskUseCase, CreateProjectUseCase and CreateUserUseCase all get IDs from the injected IdGenerator.next() (src/application/IdGenerator.ts).
Every use case returns its result through the dto.ts mappers toTaskDto, toProjectDto or toUserDto, so the conversion from domain objects to DTOs lives in one place.
AddTaskUseCase and ListTasksUseCase both delegate status parsing to the domain's parseTaskStatus and do not re-implement it.

Small duplication: AddTaskUseCase.execute and ListTasksUseCase.execute each contain `const project = await this.projects.findById(input.projectId); if (project === undefined) throw DomainError.notFound(...)`. This is a trivial guard, not a scattered invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Every file serves one concern: the task and project management use cases. Each use case class has an execute() method that coordinates domain repositories and returns DTOs. The shared support is an IdGenerator port, a TaskFinderService for looking up a task within a project, and DTO mappers in dto.ts. The abstractions are used consistently. All three create flows get IDs from the injected IdGenerator. Both task-mutation flows (assign and mark done) look up the task through TaskFinderService.findInProject and do not repeat the projectId check themselves. All use cases map their results through the dto.ts mappers. Status parsing is always delegated to the domain's parseTaskStatus. One small duplication exists: AddTaskUseCase and ListTasksUseCase both repeat the same "project must exist" check (projects.findById, then DomainError.notFound). This is a two-line guard, not a business invariant spread across the module, and nothing bypasses an existing abstraction to do it. It could be pulled into a ProjectFinder, but it is not serious enough to fail the unit. parseDueDate is defined only once, in AddTaskUseCase. No file mixes in an unrelated concern.
